First off, its such a shame that this game released in such an unoptimized and microtransaction ragebait joke of a state. I avoided it like the plague due to the things I hate most about gaming. Microtransactions in a solo video game, for mechanic based things like fast travel? Absolutely not.

However 2 whole years later I decided to give it a go, as it was on sale. This has easily become my favourite game of all time. The devs have locked in, cured optimization, removed silly microtransactions and included lots of QoL changes.

The story is okay, the movement mechanics can be frustrating and slow moving dialogue is jarring. But, something about how this game is designed not only made me slow down to make the most out of every moment but also had me very, very invested. There's a plethora of content including side quests, exploration, customisation, easily hot swappable combat styles/classes - the list goes on.

Its so rare for a game to grip me like this and moreover, there is a HUGE DLC releasing along with hard mode.

Capcom have really pulled it back, good on them.

The game is great when its doing what it does best: Combat and exploration.
Really not worth full price but grab it in a sale.

In short, regarding the multitude of bad reviews
Microtransaction
For those who mentioned about the micro-transaction issue, Art of Metamorphosis is a one time change for the appearance of your character. There will probably be a Secret of Metamorphosis that you can exchange by using Rift Crystal which is also offered as a micro-transaction, but you can earn Rift Crystals by having people rent your pawn. The only micro-transaction that can't be earned in-game is the original soundtrack.

Performance issues
It happened for MHW, the lack of optimization and very bad launch but the devs eventually fixed it and it became one of their best selling game and beloved by the community. Tbh, DDDA also had their issues with the network and etc when its released in Steam. Hence, I'm sure that Capcom will take into account of this situation and give us an explanation and solution to the problems.

Denuvo and etc
Well, I can't vouch for them regarding this. Yeah prevent piracy and all that, but it's bad.

Anyways, for the vets we have been waiting for so long, in time it will be all better. For people who never tried DDDA and got this but face many issues, have faith in Capcom. They are an amazing developer and they will fix it!

Because who doesn't want to make friends with a giant fire-breathing lizard? This game lets you fulfill your lifelong dream of befriending dragons while also reminding you that not all mythical creatures appreciate being poked with a sword. Capcom made a messy (storytelling wise) gem, with a much better combat system and sandbox mechanics than the first game. DD2 brings you innovative ways to deal with your enemies and a variety of vocations (classes) that each specialize in a different way of playing the game; but ultimately it brings you closure through your Pawns that will forever aid you in your quest to defeat the Dragon's Dogma.

I understand a lot of the hate criticism this game received.
This was a bare bones single step up away from the original.
For some, it is a massive step down.
For others, it is just a step up.
What does it come down to?
Ultimately, it comes down to difficulty.
This entry is easier than the previous one in many ways.
If you're interested in this game because you like a challenge, i say look elsewhere.

If you played the first game, it's going to be a toss up whether or not you'll enjoy this game.

The problem lies in that this game is much more beginner friendly. The other problem is they went too big on the world. It feels partially like a walking simulator with some combat. the combat isn't nearly as challenging or punishing as it was in the first one. the graphics are still good the followers are still super annoying but occasionally helpful. climbing onto monsters is still a part of the combat and that's one of the two reasons I will always give this series a chance. The other is the character customization. It makes almost all other customization options in other games leaving you with wanting more. the quests offer little in helping you accomplish their objectives.

I think more people should at least try this game. If it's too easy, pick up the first one. If you're on the fence, wait for a sale.

Do not buy. I got tricked by the fun initial gameplay, but the quests are god awful and combat gets stale. Every fight plays out the same, when you eventually run out of "creative" ways to fight the same enemy you've seen 500 times.

Exploration has too much worthless content, with the occasional gear drop you can't use every 3 hours.
Quest are unbelievably bad for a 2024 RPG, and the NPCs are so lifeless you wouldn't believe your eyes, even the ones in the main quest.

Not to mention when you actually do the quests themselves, going from a to b with basically zero consequences or impactful choices, besides having a set timer.
Which doesn't mean anything anyway when you basically get a minimum of 1 whole day, even on time sensitive quests like saving a child who got kidnapped by wolves.

This is by no means worth the price tag, even if the performance was good, the focus would then go on how little you can actually do in this supposed innovating sequel.
